analysis:
Both changed files are documentation only (docs/architecture/hardware-support.md, docs/architecture/inference.md). No source, key handling, attestation, wire protocol or authorization code changes in the supplied units, so no concrete security regression or invalidated threat assumption was found.

What the docs now describe (the code is not supplied, so none of it is verified):
- hardware-support.md lines 35-41: local HTTP Responses retain host JSON. The history LRU is bounded, but the SDK response-object store has no matching eviction. This is a possible memory-growth DoS on the local HTTP surface (related: T-016, T-029). It is documented as an accepted limit and is not coordinator-reachable on the evidence supplied.
- hardware-support.md 109-148, inference.md 71-313: GLM5Next admission, memory pricing, wired-residency fault retention, and a media/video decode path with a 512 MiB decoded-frame cap. This is described as new native attack surface (TB-007, A-001).
- inference.md ~301-304: an unproven retirement retains owners and quarantines GLM work, which fails closed rather than weakening a control.
- inference.md 1228-1253: MiMo original tool schemas are restored; reserved schema metadata is rejected.
- inference.md ~1501: a malformed GLM tool suffix fails before any call is published.
- inference.md line 61: a refused SSD store's typed reason reaches the bridge for local /metrics only. This does not touch T-041 at-rest posture, TTL, HMAC names or salt scoping, and exposes nothing to the coordinator.

For later passes: if source diffs accompany these docs, check the GLM video/MP4 decode bounds, the unbounded local response-object store, the TB-007 and T-050 plaintext-media handling for new video paths (whether decoded frames or temp files touch disk), and whether the T-041 prefix-cache assumptions still hold for GLM complete-prefix checkpoint storage identity (storage.executionPolicy). None of these are verified here.
